text: {"components": [{"type": "claim", "quote": "Switzerland autonomously introduced, and incorporated into national law through the Law on Technical Barriers to Trade, the «Cassis de Dijon principle», which was developed by the European Court of Justice.", "gist": "Switzerland adopted the Cassis de Dijon principle into its national law via the Law on Technical Barriers to Trade."}, {"type": "claim", "quote": "The «Cassis de Dijon principle» stipulates that a product which complies with the technical regulations of the EU, a member state of the EU or that of the EEA, and is legally placed on the market in one of these member states, may in principle be placed on the Swiss market without any further controls (art. 16a of the Law on Technical Barriers to Trade).", "gist": "Products legally marketed in the EU, an EU member state, or an EEA state can be sold in Switzerland without additional checks."}, {"type": "condition", "quote": "Exceptions to the principle are only possible when overriding public interests are at stake.", "gist": "Exceptions to the Cassis de Dijon principle are allowed only if overriding public interests are involved."}]}
